subject: PSHE
source: National Curriculum / statutory guidance (Relationships Education and Health Education only); PSHE Association programme of study themes; TGA RSHE Policy 2026-27 and TGA Tarbiyyah Compass Character Framework 2026-27 (Drive); Drive PSHE folder (PSHE Association KS3 'Healthy coping strategies' lesson) adapted for Y8. No RSE or sex education in Years 1 to 6 (owner decision, October 2026): body-safety safeguarding only, taught at a non-sexual level.

lessons.title: Families and the people who care for us
objectives: Say that families can be different but all care

keywords.def: people who look after each other
something that is not the same
to look after and be kind

starter: Name one way to show care.
Who can you tell if you feel unsafe?

teach.heading: Different families
bullets: Some families are big, some small
All families can care for children
teach.note: Be sensitive: avoid asking about individual family structures. Use storybook examples. The aim is respect without judging. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: How families care
bullets: They teach us right from wrong
teach.note: Ask pupils to think of ways. Examples of families: one parent, grandparents caring for children, step-families, foster or kafala families. Misconception: a family that looks different from mine cannot be a caring family.

teach.heading: Caring in return
bullets: Be kind and obedient in good
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 17:23 tells us to be kind to parents. Link to ways a child can help.

teach.heading: Respect for all
bullets: We do not make fun of differences
teach.note: Role-play: someone says 'that's weird'. What can we say instead?

practice: Name two ways a family can care for a child.
independent: Think of three ways you can help at home.
Role-play saying something kind when someone is different.
exit: Draw a picture of caring for someone in your family.
Write one sentence about how families care.
homework: Do all families look the same?
Name one way to show respect.
lessons.send: Do three helpful jobs at home and tell us next time.

lessons.title: Keep trying: resilience (sabr)
objectives: Explain that mistakes help us learn
Show perseverance when something is hard

keywords.def: keeping going when things are hard
patience and steadiness when facing difficulty
something that did not go right

starter: Name one way to help at home.

teach.heading: Tarbiyyah Compass value: Resilience
bullets: Resilience is one of our six Tarbiyyah Compass values
In Islam we call this sabr
teach.note: Introduce the value. Ask: what is hard for you? Everyone finds something hard. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Mistakes help us learn
teach.note: Tell a story of a hard task. Misconception: clever people never make mistakes.

teach.heading: Growing from hard things
bullets: Break a task into small steps
teach.note: Practise with a real puzzle or a tricky drawing. Praise effort not just the result.

teach.heading: Making dua when it is hard
bullets: We can ask Allah for help
Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity
teach.note: Qur'an 2:286 says Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear. Explain simply.

practice: What do we say when we start a task?
independent: Try a tricky shape drawing and try again if it goes wrong.
Tell a partner one thing you found hard and what helped.
exit: Draw a picture of someone trying again.
lessons.send: Practise something hard at home for five minutes each day.

lessons.title: Keeping clean and healthy
objectives: Explain why we wash hands and make wudu
Describe healthy habits: sleep, food, exercise

keywords.def: tiny living things that can make us ill

starter: Why do we wash our hands?

teach.heading: Clean hands
teach.note: Do the 20-second count together. Link: Islam encourages cleanliness. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said cleanliness is half of faith (Sahih Muslim). Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Wudu and health
bullets: Wudu cleans hands, face, arms and feet
Brushing teeth is also sunnah and healthy
teach.note: Do not teach prayer rulings; link to what children already know. Teach brushing teeth twice a day.

teach.heading: Food and sleep
teach.note: Healthy eating is balance, not strict. Ask about breakfast. Do not shame anyone's food choices.

teach.heading: Move and play
teach.note: Link to PE lesson about heart and breathing. Plan a healthy day with a timeline.

practice: How long should we wash our hands?
independent: Count slowly to 20 while washing hands.
exit: Draw your healthy day: morning, afternoon, evening.
Label one thing for hygiene, food, sleep and exercise.
homework: Why do we wash our hands?
lessons.send: Wash hands properly and brush teeth twice a day for a week; tick a chart.

lessons.title: Online: personal information and strangers
objectives: Know not to share it with strangers online
Tell a trusted adult about requests

keywords.def: details like your name, address, school and photos
just for you and trusted people
to give others to see or use

starter: Bismillah. What do we do before we click?
Name one thing you should not share online.

teach.heading: What is personal information?
teach.note: Ask: would you tell a stranger on the street? The same applies online. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Strangers online
bullets: Online people may not be who they say
A friendly name does not mean a friend
Games and chats can have strangers
teach.note: Misconception: if they are friendly they are safe. Keep explanation calm without scaring children.

teach.heading: Say no and tell
teach.note: Practise a script: 'I am not allowed to say. I will ask a grown-up.' Rehearse with a puppet.

teach.heading: Safe sharing
bullets: Use a nickname, not your real name
teach.note: Parents must allow accounts. Remind that most apps need users to be 13 or over.

practice: Name two pieces of personal information.
independent: Role-play saying no to a stranger.
exit: Make a poster listing private information.
Write three steps for 'say no and tell'.
homework: Why do we not share personal information?
What do you do if a stranger messages you?
lessons.send: Check with a grown-up what you are allowed to share online.
